Undergraduate Tuition Fees - International Students 2026/27 Show Hide Undergraduate tuition fees for international students vary depending on your programme of study (also called an 'undergraduate degree course'). See table below. Paying your deposit You're required to pay a deposit equal to 50% of your net tuition fee before you can apply for your Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS), a mandatory document for your Student Visa application. The net tuition fee is calculated after deducting any University scholarships from the gross fee. Following registration on your programme of study, the remaining balance of your net tuition fee will be payable in three equal instalments: Students starting in September A 50% deposit is due, with three equal instalments to be paid on 1 November, 1 January and 1 March. For example, if you're enrolled on a course with a gross tuition fee of £16,950 and you receive an International Scholarship of £3,000, your net tuition fee becomes £13,950. Consequently, your deposit will be 50% of £13,950: £6,975. The remaining balance will then be divided into three equal payments of £2,325 each. Please note: In certain circumstances, if risk factors are identified in relation to visa applications, a student may be required to pay either the full first-year tuition fee or a higher deposit prior to the issuance of the CAS. Should this occur, you'll be advised accordingly. Exceptions You are required to pay 100% deposit before you can apply for your CAS if you legally reside in: Afghanistan. Iran. Pakistan. Bangladesh. The Indian states of Punjab, Haryana, Gujarat, and Telangana. Applicants who legally reside in Nigeria need to pay a flat deposit of £4,500. If you pay your full deposit by 1 June 2026, you will qualify for the Early Bird discount. See 'Early Bird and upfront payment discounts' below. Early Bird and upfront payment discounts These discounts apply to international students on undergraduate and postgraduate taught programmes only. They do not apply to postgraduate research. They apply to students starting for the first time in September 2026 or January 2027, not continuing students. How they work: Discounts apply to your net tuition fee only (the fee after any scholarships). The 3% Early Bird 50% deposit discount applies to your first year of study only. The 5% Early Bird remaining fees discount applies to each year of your course where you pay in full by the deadline. The 5% Early Bird will not be applied to additional study years caused by resits. The maximum discount in any year is 5%. If you meet both deadlines, you receive 5%, not 8%. Students who do not require a student visa You can either pay fees in full or set up a monthly payment plan. You can set up a monthly payment plan during the online registration process. For more information on your payment options, please read our Student Debt Management Policy . Sponsor Funding If you are an overseas student requiring a student visa, and your sponsor is on the University’s approved list ( see appendix B of the Student Debt Management Policy ), your sponsor will be invoiced after registration. In all other cases, the sponsor must pay your tuition fees in full before you can register. Paying Tuition Fees Log onto the intranet – please do not share your log in details with anyone else, in accordance with University regulations. Go to the MyFinance section . Click on the option 'Pre-payment of Tuition fees (Overseas applicants only)'. This will take you to our international payment system. Full instructions on how to make your payment are provided on this system. Remaining tuition fees and fees for all other student fee categories are made during online registration. sections.text: Postgraduate Tuition Fees - International Students 2026/27 Show Hide Postgraduate tuition fees for international students vary depending on your programme of study (also called a 'postgraduate degree course'). See table below. Paying your deposit You’re required to pay a deposit equal to 50% of your net tuition fee before you can apply for your Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) – a mandatory document for your Student Visa application. The net tuition fee is calculated after deducting any University scholarships from the gross fee. Following registration on your programme of study, the remaining balance of your net tuition fee will be payable in three equal instalments: Students starting in September A 50% deposit is due, with three equal instalments to be paid on 1 November, 1 January and 1 March. Students starting in January A 50% deposit is due, with three equal instalments to be paid on 1 March, 1 May and 1 July. For example, if you’re enrolled on a course with a gross tuition fee of £18,950 and you receive an International Scholarship of £3,000, your net tuition fee becomes £15,950. Consequently, your deposit will be 50% of £15,950—that is, £7,975. The remaining balance will then be divided into three equal payments of £2,658.33 each. Please note: In certain circumstances, if risk factors are identified in relation to visa applications, a student may be required to pay either the full first-year tuition fee or a higher deposit prior to the issuance of the CAS. Should this occur, you’ll be advised accordingly. Exceptions You are required to pay 100% deposit before you can apply for your CAS if you legally reside in: Afghanistan. Iran. Pakistan. Bangladesh. The Indian states of Punjab, Haryana, Gujarat, and Telangana. Applicants who legally reside in Nigeria need to pay a flat deposit of £4500. If you pay your full deposit by 1 June, you will qualify for the early bird discount. Early Bird Discount and upfront payment discounts These discounts apply to international students on undergraduate and postgraduate taught programmes only. They do not apply to postgraduate research. They apply to students starting for the first time in September 2026 or January 2027, not continuing students. How they work: Discounts apply to your net tuition fee only (the fee after any scholarships). The 3% Early Bird 50% deposit discount applies to your first year of study only. sections.text: Postgraduate Tuition Fees - International Students 2026/27 Show Hide Postgraduate tuition fees for international students vary depending on your programme of study (also called a 'postgraduate degree course'). See table below. Paying your deposit You’re required to pay a deposit equal to 50% of your net tuition fee before you can apply for your Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) – a mandatory document for your Student Visa application. The net tuition fee is calculated after deducting any University scholarships from the gross fee. Following registration on your programme of study, the remaining balance of your net tuition fee will be payable in three equal instalments: Students starting in September A 50% deposit is due, with three equal instalments to be paid on 1 November, 1 January and 1 March. Students starting in January A 50% deposit is due, with three equal instalments to be paid on 1 March, 1 May and 1 July. For example, if you’re enrolled on a course with a gross tuition fee of £18,950 and you receive an International Scholarship of £3,000, your net tuition fee becomes £15,950. Consequently, your deposit will be 50% of £15,950—that is, £7,975. The remaining balance will then be divided into three equal payments of £2,658.33 each. Please note: In certain circumstances, if risk factors are identified in relation to visa applications, a student may be required to pay either the full first-year tuition fee or a higher deposit prior to the issuance of the CAS. Should this occur, you’ll be advised accordingly. Exceptions You are required to pay 100% deposit before you can apply for your CAS if you legally reside in: Afghanistan. Iran. Pakistan. Bangladesh. The Indian states of Punjab, Haryana, Gujarat, and Telangana. Applicants who legally reside in Nigeria need to pay a flat deposit of £4500. If you pay your full deposit by 1 June, you will qualify for the early bird discount. Early Bird Discount and upfront payment discounts These discounts apply to international students on undergraduate and postgraduate taught programmes only. They do not apply to postgraduate research. They apply to students starting for the first time in September 2026 or January 2027, not continuing students.
